page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg5.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical Intel Xeon 6149 cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, translating to 4.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average multi-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests. Single-core performance is relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25% across stress-ng and Geekbench single-core metrics. Memory bandwidth presents a mixed profile, with average performance on small-block cached reads and large-block writes, but weak performance on large-block uncached reads. Cryptographic and vector processing capabilities are supported by AVX, AVX-512F, and AES instructions, yielding average results in Passmark extended instructions and encryption tests.

Given the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this instance is suited for general-purpose workloads such as software compilation, text processing, and moderate Redis key-value operations, which show average benchmark throughput. However, it is less optimal for memory-intensive database operations, static web serving, or complex image processing due to lower benchmark scores in those areas. Large-scale LLM inference is also constrained, with poor performance on 7B models, though small-model prompt processing remains functional at average speeds.
